chunks: And Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who hires a porter, and he breaks what he is carrying upon him or spills it, he said: “If he is trustworthy, then there is nothing upon him; and if he is not trustworthy, then he is liable.”

key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally liable for loss or damage
key_terms.غَيْرَ مَأْمُونٍ: not trustworthy or not reliable in custody
key_terms.مَأْمُونًا: trustworthy and relied upon in safeguarding the property
key_terms.يُهَرِيقُهُ: he spills it or pours it out
key_terms.ٱلْحَمَّالَ: a porter or carrier hired to transport goods

ai.seo_question: Is a hired porter liable if he breaks or spills the goods he was carrying?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the liability of a hired porter who damages or spills entrusted goods. The ruling distinguishes between a trustworthy worker and one who is not trustworthy: the trustworthy one is not held liable, while the untrustworthy one is held responsible.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3931 - Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (as),

regarding a man who hires a porter, and the porter either breaks what he is carrying or spills it.
Imam (as) said: "If he is trustworthy, then he is not liable. But if he is not trustworthy, then he is liable."
